Right: the same graph without the edge from D back to C (drawn dashed in the accent color); nothing in D, E, F can reach A, B, C, so is_strongly_connected() returns False." width="100%"} A directed graph is strongly connected if there is a directed path from every node to every other node. Equivalently, the graph has exactly one strongly connected component containing all nodes. For undirected graphs, this is equivalent to checking regular connectivity (same as `is_connected()`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is strongly connected, `False` otherwise. Empty graphs are considered strongly connected (vacuously true). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Returns `True` iff the entire node set forms a single SCC, delegating to the same Kosaraju pass as `strongly_connected_components()` and short-circuiting once a second component is discovered, so the effective cost is $O(V + E)$. Empty graphs are treated as trivially strongly connected, matching the vacuously-true convention that pairs of nonexistent nodes need no path. On undirected graphs strong and ordinary connectivity coincide, so this call falls through to `is_connected()` semantics. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a directed cycle, every node can reach every other node by following the arrows around: ::: {#24d6b64f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) # Returns True graph.is_strongly_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Adding a node that can only be reached one-way breaks strong connectivity, even though the rest of the graph is still tightly connected: ::: {#72e569ff .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.add_node(label="D") graph.add_edge("D", "A") # D can reach A, but nothing can reach D # Returns False graph.is_strongly_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: :::
